### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, completion of A28 followed completion of A21 after about 0.92 hours on average (median about 0.91 h, middle 50% roughly 0.84–0.99 h). In the later window, this elapsed time is about 0.45 hours (median about 0.45 h, middle 50% roughly 0.41–0.50 h) — roughly half, with a visibly narrower spread (std about 0.12 h → 0.07 h). The pair occurred at a similar rate in both windows, in about 50 in 100 traces (101 vs 104 occurrences). [TWAIT001]
- Completion of A28 followed completion of A29 after about 0.18 hours on average (median about 0.15 h) in the earlier window, and about 0.09 hours (median about 0.08 h) in the later window — also roughly half, again with a narrower spread (std about 0.13 h → 0.07 h). This pair also occurred in about 50 in 100 traces in both windows (99 vs 96 occurrences). [TWAIT002]
- Both timing differences are larger than in about 1999 of 2000 random re-splits of the pooled data. These are the only items that qualified overall: 2 time items against roughly 0.009 expected by chance among 19 time units, while control flow produced no items (0 among 54 units, about 0.27 expected by chance). [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in timing around A28: in the later window, the elapsed time between consecutive completion events leading into A28 is roughly halved, both from A21 (about 0.92 h → 0.45 h on average) and from A29 (about 0.18 h → 0.09 h on average). Supporting signs: both items measure these elapsed times directly, agree in direction, rest on about 100 observations per window, exceed about 1999 of 2000 random re-splits, and together far exceed the chance expectation for the time family; the absence of control-flow items is consistent with a timing change, which needs no structural counterpart. Limitations: TWAIT is elapsed time between consecutive completion events, so the evidence cannot show whether A28 itself completed sooner, the predecessors completed earlier, or less time simply passed in between; and because both items share A28, they may reflect one underlying timing change rather than two independent ones. A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is a shift in which events fall consecutively (different interleaving), which would change the elapsed times being measured; the stable occurrence rates of both pairs (about 50 in 100 traces in each window) argue against this but do not exclude it. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]

Other differences: none qualified at the configured thresholds; no control-flow, participation or ordering differences were observed. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]
